title: How to Fix Disconnected & Backward Arabic Text in Photoshop (2026 Guide)
excerpt: Struggling with isolated Arabic letters or backward text in Photoshop? Learn how to enable World-Ready Layout and RTL paragraph rules in under 2 minutes.

content:
If you're designing marketing banners, social media assets, or localized graphics in Adobe Photoshop, encountering isolated, disconnected Arabic letters or text typing completely in reverse is one of the most frustrating bottlenecks. Instead of flowing smoothly from right to left with connected cursive script, your text appears as separate glyphs flowing left to right—for example, rendering ع ر ب ي instead of عربي.

This behavior is not caused by a corrupted font file or a broken installation. It simply means Photoshop's text layout engine is defaulting to Western Left-to-Right (LTR) paragraph rules instead of multi-byte Right-to-Left (RTL) Bidirectional (BiDi) shaping.

Here is how to fix disconnected and inverted Arabic text in Photoshop natively, along with steps to restore missing Middle Eastern options in your menus.

Key Takeaways:

  • Disconnected Arabic text in Photoshop is caused by Western LTR paragraph rules, not missing font files.
  • Activate World-Ready Layout in the Paragraph panel menu to instantly connect Arabic cursive characters.
  • Toggle paragraph direction to RTL to correct reversed character typing sequence.
  • If Middle Eastern options are missing, change Creative Cloud default install language to English (Supports Arabic).

The Direct Solution: Enable Middle Eastern Features & World-Ready Layout

Since Photoshop 23.0 (and continuing through Photoshop 2025 and 2026), Adobe uses a consolidated core called the Unified Text Engine.

You no longer need to switch engine preferences globally in the main application settings. Instead, you control text rendering directly through the Paragraph and Character panels.

Step 1: Set Paragraph Direction to Right-to-Left (RTL)

A common mistake designers make is clicking the "Right Align" button in the top options bar. Right alignment changes where the text sits on your canvas, but it does not change how characters flow.

  1. Select your text layer or highlight the broken Arabic text block with the Type Tool (T).
  2. Open the Paragraph Panel by going to Window → Paragraph.
  3. Click the Right-to-Left Paragraph Direction button (the icon showing an arrow pointing left over horizontal lines).

Step 2: Activate the World-Ready Paragraph Composer

If your characters are still standing isolated after setting the direction to RTL, Photoshop is using the standard single-line composer which cannot process Arabic ligature connections.

  1. In the Paragraph Panel, click the flyout menu icon (the four horizontal lines in the top-right corner).
  2. Select World-Ready Layout (or Adobe World-Ready Paragraph Composer).
  3. Your Arabic text will immediately join into natural, connected cursive script.

What to Do If Middle Eastern Options Are Missing from Photoshop

If you open the Paragraph panel flyout menu and cannot find the Right-to-Left direction toggles or World-Ready options, your Adobe Creative Cloud app was installed using a Western-only language build.

You can fix this in under two minutes without losing your brush sets or workspace presets.

  1. Save your open projects and close Photoshop.
  2. Open the Adobe Creative Cloud Desktop App.
  3. Click your profile avatar in the upper-right corner and select Preferences.
  4. Navigate to the Apps tab on the left sidebar.
  5. Scroll down to Default Install Language and change the dropdown menu to English (Supports Arabic) or English (Supports Hebrew).
  6. Relaunch Photoshop. The Middle Eastern features, right-to-left direction buttons, and Arabic dictionaries will now appear automatically under Type → Language Options.

Choosing Arabic-Compatible OpenType Fonts

Even with correct engine settings, using legacy TrueType (.ttf) font files designed before modern Unicode standards can result in misaligned diacritics or awkward character spacing.

For clean, professional results in print and digital media, use verified OpenType or WOFF2 font families:

  • Google Fonts (Free / Commercial Use): Cairo, Tajawal, Amiri, Readex Pro, El Messiri, Alexandria.
  • Adobe Fonts: Adobe Arabic, Myriad Arabic, Greta Arabic, Noto Naskh.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why doesn't right-aligning paragraph text connect Arabic letters?

Right-aligning only shifts the text position relative to the canvas boundary. Connecting cursive Arabic glyphs requires active RTL paragraph direction rules and the Adobe World-Ready Paragraph Composer.

Do I need to reinstall Photoshop to get Middle Eastern features?

No full reinstallation is necessary. Simply update your default install language to "English (Supports Arabic)" inside Creative Cloud Desktop preferences and relaunch Photoshop.
